newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends mixed ahead of U.S. elections.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends mixed ahead of U.S. elections.

text.p: The dollar ended mixed Monday in quiet, mostly featureless trading ahead of the presidential and congressional elections on Tuesday.

"It's a very docile, quiet day," said Tom Benfer, director of foreign exchange at Bank of Montreal. "I think it's keeping people on the sidelines from taking big positions," he said, referring to the elections.
Polls showed President Clinton ahead of challenger Bob Dole in the presidential race, while many key races in the fight for control of the House and Senate were too close to call.
The dollar rose to 113.80 Japanese yen late in New York, from 113.35 yen late Friday. The dollar fell to 1.5105 German marks from 1.5143 marks.
The dollar had sold off against the yen on Friday after former Treasury Secretary Lloyd Bentsen warned that a stronger dollar could hurt foreign demand for American exports.

As treasury secretary in the first two years of the Clinton administration, Bentsen was said to favour an informal ceiling of about 113 yen for the dollar. By contrast, current Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin has reiterated the administration's support for a strong dollar.
The dollar rebounded Monday as currency traders reconsidered Bentsen's remarks and bought back dollars.

"The dollar is ... recovering from its weakness on Friday from Lloyd Bentsen's comments seen as possibly suggesting that the administration was going to change its tone on the dollar after the election," said Chris Widness, an international economist at Chase Securities Inc.
"But I think the market is really not buying into that," Widness said. "That's why the dollar is coming back today."

The yen also weakened versus other major currencies including the mark. The Bank of Japan has kept official interest rates at rock-bottom levels to help stimulate economic growth in Japan. Low rates hurt the Japanese currency by making yen-denominated deposits less attractive.

"There's been a lot of demand for marks for yen today and the demand to buy Deutschemarks has weighed on the dollar (against the mark) and kept dollar versus yen up as well," said William Marr, manager of foreign exchange at Credit Commerciale De France.
The British pound climbed against most leading currencies, including the dollar, the mark and the yen, after falling over the weekend.
Traders initially bet that the $20 billion British Telecommunications-MCI Communications merger announced on Sunday would boost demand for dollars in Britain.
But Widness said traders realised that was not likely as regulators will take months to review the deal before it can be completed.
The pound touched $1.6470, a fresh 20-month high, and settled at $1.6453, up from $1.6360 late Friday.
The dollar fell to 1.2662 Swiss francs from 1.2695 francs. It rose to Canadian $1.3361 from C$1.3340.
